cohort: The study included 28.7 million pregnancy-related hospitalizations from the National Inpatient Sample database (2012-2018), specifically identifying 51,200 pregnant women with HBV and 131,695 with HCV.
finding: Compared to uninfected controls, pregnant women with HBV were more likely to develop gestational diabetes, while those with HCV were more likely to experience preterm labor, intrauterine growth restriction, longer length of stay, and higher hospitalization costs.
